newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police raid 60 houses for child porn.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police raid 60 houses for child porn.

text.p: Belgian police searching for paedophile pornography and child porn networks raided 60 homes and other establishments around the country in a coordinated operation on Thursday, a Brussels Court spokesman said.
"Based on a list of addresses we received from France and another from Great Britain we carried out searches at 60 or so places today," spokesman Josef Colpin told Reuters.
He said about 20 of the searches were at addresses in and around Brussels, with the rest scattered throughout the country.
Colpin declined to give any details of what, if any, material had been seized or if any arrests had been made.

Belgium has been in turmoil since mid-August when convicted rapist Marc Dutroux was arrested. Two sexually-abused young girls were rescued from a dungeon in one of his houses and police subsequently discovered the buried bodies of four more.
Eight-year-olds Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo had been missing since June 1995. Dutroux said they starved to death early last year.

Their bodies were found next to that of a former Dutroux accomplice, Frenchman Bernard Weinstein, on another property belonging to Dutroux in Sars-La-Buissiere, south-west of the central city of Charleroi.
Dutroux, paroled in 1992 after serving only three years of a 13-year sentence for multiple child rape, has admitted murdering Weinstein.
The bodies of teenagers An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks, missing for a year, were unearthed in early September at another property in Charleroi connected with Dutroux.

Police on Thursday ended a fruitless three-week underground search at an abandoned coal mining complex in the city, where they have been looking for signs of several other missing children, including bodies.

They have been working on their own information and on statements by Dutroux and his second wife Michelle Martin, who is also under arrest along with three other suspects. Searches will continue next week above ground at the site.
A special parliamentary commission is investigating the handling of the searches for the dead girls.
Its chairman, Marc Verwilghen, said earlier this week it was obvious that, had it not been for bungling by police and magistrates, the girls would be alive today.

There have been allegations that the Dutroux gang was only able to operate for so long -- despite the fact he himself was under secret surveillance by gendarmes -- because he had high-level protection.

Last October more than 250,000 people marched through Brussels in a demonstration of support for victims of the paedophile ring and their parents and of general public disgust at the whole legal and political system.
Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene immediately promised wide-ranging reforms, and parents of the children met him on Thursday night to review progress.

Asked by Belgian television just before the meeting whether the government was moving fast enough, Gino Russo - Melissa's father - said, "I have to say yes, because they are not things that can be done quickly."
However An's father Paul Marchal said that for him the promised changes were taking to long to be put into effect.
